title: Finite coefficient change on henselian polynomial cylinders
statement: Let $\Lambda\hookrightarrow V$ be a finite injective local map [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], where $\Lambda,V$ are both fields or both complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $e\geq0$, put $D=\Lambda[[u_1,\ldots,u_e]]$, $E=V[[u_1,\ldots,u_e]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $S=(D[T]_{(\mathfrak m_D,T)})^h$ and $S_V=(E[T]_{(\mathfrak m_E,T)})^h$ be ordinary henselizations [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then $D,E$ are complete Noetherian local domains, $S,S_V$ are excellent Noetherian henselian local domains [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-exc-excellent-ring], and $S\to S_V$ is finite and local. Put $R=D[[T]]$ and $R_V=E[[T]]$. The canonical maps identify the maximal-ideal completions of $S,S_V$ with $R,R_V$, respectively, and the natural map $R\otimes_S S_V\to R_V$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Moreover $R_V$ is finite over $R$. If $g=T^n+\sum_{i<n}b_iT^i\in D[T]$ with $n>0$ and $b_i\in\mathfrak m_D$, then $(S,gS)$ and $(S_V,gS_V)$ are henselian pairs, and $R,R_V$ are also their respective $g$-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Both completion maps are faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: V 1.1.3, 1.2.3 and 3.2.3, pp.63--64,67: finite coefficient comparison made explicit; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-henselization), more-algebra.tex Tags 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent) and 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent).

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, local, complete for its zero maximal ideal, and a domain. A complete DVR has these properties by its definition (every ideal is principal). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain] to each coefficient ring, in $e$ variables and in $e+1$ variables. Thus $D,E,R,R_V$ are complete Noetherian local domains. Their maximal ideals consist of the series whose constant coefficient lies in the maximal ideal of the coefficient ring. Regrouping coefficients identifies the $(e+1)$-variable rings with $D[[T]],E[[T]]$: the coefficient of $u^aT^j$ is the coefficient of $u^a$ in the $T^j$ coefficient, and the finite convolution formulas for multiplication coincide. This includes $e=0$.

source.place: V 1.1.3, complete Noetherian coefficient rings; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series).

proof.text: Choose finitely many $\Lambda$-module generators $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$. For a series $F=\sum_a c_a u^a\in E$, choose expressions $c_a=\sum_i\lambda_{ia}v_i$. Then $F=\sum_i v_i(\sum_a\lambda_{ia}u^a)$; equality is coefficientwise. Consequently $E$ is finite over $D$. The same argument with the additional $T$ exponent shows directly that $R_V$ is finite over $R$. Grouping the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial shows that the same $v_i$ generate $E[T]$ over $D[T]$. Coefficientwise injectivity gives $D\hookrightarrow E$. Since $\Lambda\to V$ is local, the constant-coefficient criterion of Step 1 gives $\mathfrak m_E\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$, and hence $(\mathfrak m_E,T)\cap D[T]=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$.

source.place: V 3.2.3, comparison of the coefficient rings; explicit coefficient argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder] twice, with coefficient ring $D$ and then $E$, with $r=1$ and input $f=T$. The hypotheses hold by Step 1, and $T$ is a nonunit with nonzero reduction modulo the coefficient maximal ideal. The henselizations in that statement are exactly $S$ and $S_V$. Its conclusions give that they are Noetherian local henselian, that their canonical maximal-ideal completions are $R$ and $R_V$, and that the maps to those completions are faithfully flat. Only these conclusions are used here; its existential distinguished polynomial is not identified with the prescribed $g$.

source.place: V 1.1.3 and 2.2.3: the horizontal maps are completions for the maximal-ideal topologies.

proof.text: By [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], $D$ and $E$ are excellent. Apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] to their one-variable polynomial rings and the indicated prime localizations. These localized rings are excellent and therefore quasi-excellent by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. They are reduced: a polynomial ring over a domain has no zero divisors by the leading-coefficient formula, and localization at a prime preserves this by the fraction multiplication rule. Apply the first clause of [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation] to each of these reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian local rings. It gives excellence of $S,S_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective], applied to the base ring as its own module and its completion map from Step 3, $S\to R$ and $S_V\to R_V$ are injective (identify $A\otimes_A B$ with $B$ by multiplication). Since the targets are nonzero domains, the sources are nonzero domains as well.

source.place: V 3.2.3, excellent henselian cylinders; Stacks Tags 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent), 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent) and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: Step 2 makes $D[T]\to E[T]$ finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite], it is finite type and quasi-finite at $(\mathfrak m_E,T)$. This prime lies over $(\mathfrak m_D,T)$ by the explicit contraction calculation in Step 2. Therefore [lem-trf-henselization-quasi-finite-ring], applied to these polynomial rings and primes, gives a finite local canonical map $S\to S_V$. The maps $S\to S_V\to R_V$ and $S\to R\to R_V$ agree: both are local extensions of $D[T]_{(\mathfrak m_D,T)}\to R_V$, and uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] applies because $R_V$ is complete local and hence henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian].

source.place: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05WP (lemma-quasi-finite-henselization), not 05WR; ILO V 3.2.3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to $S\to S_V$. Any prime of $S_V$ lying over $\mathfrak m_S$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]. Since $S_V$ is local, there is precisely one such prime, namely $\mathfrak m_{S_V}$; it lies over $\mathfrak m_S$ since the map is local. Now [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension], with base $S$, finite algebra $S_V$ and prime $\mathfrak m_S$, gives $\widehat S\otimes_S S_V\cong\widehat {S_V}$. Localization at the maximal ideal changes neither local ring, and the product on the right has one factor. Substitute the canonical identifications of Step 3. Compatibility of the comparison with the $\widehat S$-algebra and $S_V$-algebra structures makes it send $a\otimes b$ to $\widehat\varphi(a)$ times the image of $b$, where $\widehat\varphi:\widehat S\to\widehat{S_V}$ is induced by $\varphi:S\to S_V$ on the quotients $S/\mathfrak m_S^k\to S_V/\mathfrak m_{S_V}^k$. Under Step 3, $S/\mathfrak m_S^k=R/\mathfrak m_R^k$ and $S_V/\mathfrak m_{S_V}^k=R_V/\mathfrak m_{R_V}^k$; by Step 5 the map on these quotients is induced by the coefficient inclusion $R\to R_V$, which is local and so maps $\mathfrak m_R^k$ into $\mathfrak m_{R_V}^k$. Taking the inverse limit over $k$, $\widehat\varphi$ is the inclusion $R\to R_V$, so the comparison sends $a\otimes b$ to $ab$. Thus it is exactly the map in the statement, not merely an abstract isomorphism. Finiteness of $R_V/R$ was already proved by generators in Step 2.

Let $g$ be as in the statement. It belongs to $\mathfrak m_S$ and to $\mathfrak m_{S_V}$: modulo the coefficient maximal ideal its image is $T^n$ with $n>0$. To check the henselian-pair assertion for either local henselian ring $H=S,S_V$, take a finite $H$-algebra $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], $B$ is a finite product of local $H$-algebras $B_j$ whose structural maps are local. Then $gB_j$ is contained in the maximal ideal, so $B_j/gB_j$ is nonzero local. In a local ring an idempotent is $0$ or $1$: from $x(1-x)=0$, one of $x,1-x$ is a unit. Thus reduction is a bijection on idempotents in every factor, and in their product, including the empty product. This is precisely [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] for $(H,gH)$.

Write $B=D$ or $E$, $A=B[T]_{(\mathfrak m_B,T)}$, $H=A^h$, and $C=B[[T]]$. For each $N\ge1$, $g^N$ is monic and reduces to $T^{nN}$. By [lem-per-distinguished-polynomial-quotient], $B[T]/(g^N)\to C/g^NC$ is the canonical isomorphism. The target is nonzero local because $g\in\mathfrak m_C$, and is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-henselian-pair]. The composite $B[T]\to C/g^NC\to C/\mathfrak m_C$ has kernel $(\mathfrak m_B,T)$. Thus every element outside that prime maps to a unit in $C/g^NC$. Localizing the displayed isomorphism gives $A/g^NA\cong C/g^NC$. In particular $A/g^NA$ is already henselian local. For $B=E$, locality of $D\to E$ ensures that all lower coefficients of $g$ lie in $\mathfrak m_E$, as required.

source.place: V Theorem 1.1.1(i), division clause, and Lemma 1.1.3, with Q=g^N.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-henselization-quotient-at-prime], $H/g^NH$ is the ordinary henselization of $A/g^NA$. The latter is henselian by Step 8, so its henselization map is an isomorphism: [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] applied to its identity gives a local retraction, and uniqueness for maps to its henselization makes the other composite the identity. Consequently the canonical map $H/g^NH\to C/g^NC$ is an isomorphism, since its composite with $A/g^NA\to H/g^NH$ is the isomorphism of Step 8. Reduction from $N+1$ to $N$ commutes with these maps, since each sends the class of $h\in H$ to the class of its fixed image in $C$.

source.place: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05WQ (lemma-quotient-henselization); ILO V Lemma 1.1.3.

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-complete-local-subideal], the complete Noetherian local ring $C$ is complete also for $gC\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. Taking inverse limits of the compatible isomorphisms of Step 9 therefore identifies $\varprojlim_N H/g^NH$ with $C$. The map from $H$ is the canonical map already used, since every inverse-limit coordinate is its reduction modulo $g^N$. With $(H,C)=(S,R)$ and $(S_V,R_V)$, this proves the two specified $g$-adic completion identifications. Their maps are the faithfully flat maps of Step 3, so all clauses hold for the same canonical maps.
